papers.text: Build Kitecombe a hill. The League currently launches from a chair.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: Make the shop awnings an official landing. Kites use them anyway.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: A topiary kite for the kite field. It never lands in hedges. It is one.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: Declare the Kitecombe maze kite-free. Kites inside may apply to leave.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: A sign over the water, facing up: KITES, PLEASE GO ROUND.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: New shears for the Committee. The anglers' willow is worried.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: Kites need the band's park. Then the bandstand. Then the tuba, for ballast.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: A spotters' gallery over the river. Pages to be turned quietly.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Pose beside a hedge clipped in your likeness. A modest hedge.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: Give the Guild the hedge show's day. The hedges have not objected.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: The Circle will pay for band practice indoors. Far indoors.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Window boxes for every shop: FLOWERS ONLY. Last year a leek got in.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: Rope off the prize beds. Last year's footprints were 40 % spotter.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: Judge the hedge show. All 212 are equally straight. Point at one.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: An inquiry into why coaches come in threes, from the Guild's window.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The coaches then came in fours. The inquiry asks for a fourth window.

papers.text: Ride the first coach of spring. You will be logged as luggage.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Hold the parsnip show in the coach park. Parked coaches are entered.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A committee to pick a tune, on the kite field. It will hear every tune first.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The tune committee heard every tune. Now it asks for an encore.

papers.text: A bandstand at the heart of the maze. Audiences will find it, in time.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: The band will pay for a licence to echo. Anglers hear each tune twice.
papers.subject: paperwork

papers.text: Lend the Guild the founding napkin. Ironing it may amend the law.
papers.subject: paperwork

papers.text: Let the League file its spare string in the hedges. Under S.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: A study of silence by the water. The band may give evidence, in writing.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The band's evidence filled nine volumes. The study asks for a reading room.

papers.text: We will pay to log the kite festival. Each kite, then each string.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: An inquiry into why kites pick hedges. The witness is still up one.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The witness will not come down. The inquiry asks to sit in the hedge too.

papers.text: Be photographed waving from every coach. I have booked four hundred.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: The growers fill cans at our pond. May we sit by their rain barrel?
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: A hat for you. And one for your coach. And for each wheel, perhaps?
papers.subject: hats

favour.text: About the hat: it asks to be logged by the spotters as a coach.

clippings.sign: SPOTTERS TOLD TO LOG A HAT; HAT RUNS LATE
clippings.refuse: HAT IS NOT A COACH, PRESIDENT RULES

papers.text: The Guild will pay for a quiet day. Each tune rattles eleven panes.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Rodney wants your name in every hedge. The last president stopped at initials.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: Make the riverbank BANDSTAND (TEMPORARY) on weekdays. Anglers become audience.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Survey the hedges with kite string, pulled tight. The League lends it.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The string is not straight. The survey asks to survey the string.

papers.text: We will pay to grow beans up the hedges. Straight beans score 20 % higher.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: Lend the spotters a shop window. Coaches look better framed.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Sit for the prize cabbage's portrait. You will be in the background.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: The League will hire the coach station roof: 11 % nearer the sky.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: A fruit basket, as before. A ribbon on it, as before. No reason.
papers.subject: ribbons

favour.text: About the basket: it would like a shop window. The Guild's best one.

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT'S BASKET TAKES GUILD'S BEST WINDOW
clippings.refuse: BASKET REFUSED A WINDOW; TO BE EATEN INSTEAD

papers.text: A working group on the tomato question. It will sit on the spotters' bench.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The tomato is undecided. The group asks to sit another summer.

papers.text: A bird bath for you. With a spout, a fountain. With two, a better one.
papers.subject: fountains

favour.text: About the bird bath: it asks to enter the Quiet Competition. It drips.

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT'S BIRD BATH ENTERS QUIET COMPETITION; DRIPS
clippings.refuse: BIRD BATH STAYS ON LAWN, STILL NOT A FOUNTAIN

papers.text: The Committee will pay to trim the coach stop hedge. It is 12 % spotter-shaped.
papers.subject: hedges
